quiz.prompt: Google MLOps level 1 adds:
quiz.explain: Level 1 automates the training pipeline (CT); level 2 automates the pipeline's own CI/CD.

quiz.prompt: Train/serve skew is:
options: Features computed differently at training and serving time
quiz.explain: Same raw input, different feature values -> silently worse predictions.

quiz.prompt: In MLOps, CD delivers:
options: A training pipeline and/or model service, not just code
quiz.explain: The deployable unit includes data/model/pipeline.

quiz.prompt: Why is 'retrain manually when someone notices' MLOps level 0?
rubric: Manual, script/notebook-driven, no automated pipeline or CT.
Infrequent releases, no monitoring-triggered retraining, disconnect between DS and ops.
Names what moving to level 1 would automate.

practice.title: 20 tracked runs, promoted by alias
practice.brief: No-card path: local MLflow server (`mlflow server --backend-store-uri sqlite:///mlflow.db`) - no cloud. Track 20 runs of a sklearn model (params, metrics, artifacts, git SHA tag), register the best, set alias `champion`, load it via `models:/name@champion` in a separate script.

quiz.prompt: A model registry adds over plain artifact logging:
options: Versioned, named models with lifecycle stages/aliases
quiz.explain: Registry = catalogue + versions + promotion workflow.

quiz.prompt: Loading an untrusted pickle file is dangerous because:
quiz.explain: pickle can reconstruct arbitrary objects, including ones that run code; prefer safetensors/ONNX/skops for untrusted sources.

quiz.prompt: Which should be logged per run?
options: Params, metrics, code version, data version and artifacts
Nothing if the code is in git
quiz.explain: Everything needed to reproduce and compare.

quiz.prompt: Why reference a model by alias (e.g. `champion`) instead of a version number in serving code?
rubric: Promotion/rollback becomes a registry change, not a code change/redeploy.
Decouples deployment from model iteration; auditable alias moves.
Notes the need to pin/log the resolved version at load time for traceability.

practice.title: Monthly training flow with backfill
practice.brief: No-card path: Prefect server runs locally (`prefect server start`); no Prefect Cloud needed. Flow: download(month) -> features -> train -> log to MLflow, with task retries=2 and a monthly schedule. Backfill three past months.
practice.done_when: Prefect UI shows 3 backfill runs; re-running the same month overwrites the same output path (no duplicates) - proven by listing outputs; flow takes `year, month` parameters and never calls `today()`.

quiz.prompt: A backfill:
options: Re-runs a pipeline for past intervals
quiz.explain: Used after bug fixes or for new pipelines needing history.

quiz.prompt: A task is idempotent if:
options: Re-running it with the same inputs yields the same result without piling up side effects
quiz.explain: E.g. overwrite partition output instead of appending.

quiz.prompt: ELT differs from ETL by:
options: Loading raw data first, then transforming in the warehouse
quiz.explain: Cheap warehouse compute made transform-after-load common.

quiz.prompt: Why pass the data period as a flow parameter instead of using `today()` inside the code?
rubric: Enables backfills and re-runs of any interval.
Deterministic/idempotent runs; testable.
Scheduler supplies the logical date; avoids timezone/late-run bugs.

practice.title: Quarantine bad rows
practice.brief: No-card path: all local. Add a Pandera validation task to the U04 flow. Inject 2% nulls and out-of-range trip durations.
practice.done_when: Run log shows N rows quarantined to `quarantine/<month>.parquet` with a failure-case report, the flow continues on clean rows, and a separate test proves a missing column fails the run fast.

quiz.prompt: A schema check catches:
options: Wrong types, missing columns, out-of-range values
quiz.explain: Schema/value checks are structural; drift needs distribution comparison.

quiz.prompt: Quarantining bad rows instead of failing the run suits:
options: High-volume feeds where a few bad rows should not block everything
quiz.explain: When correctness of the aggregate is critical, fail fast instead.

quiz.prompt: Data checks belong:
options: At ingestion, before training, and on serving inputs
quiz.explain: Bad data can enter at every boundary.

quiz.prompt: Give one data bug a schema check cannot catch, and how you would catch it.
rubric: Example: valid-looking but wrong values (unit change, label shift, duplicated days, distribution drift).
Catch with distribution/drift tests, reconciliation counts, or business-rule checks across rows/time.

practice.title: CI + CT with a champion/challenger gate
practice.brief: No-card path: GitHub Actions (free for public repos) + LocalStack/MinIO; CD deploys to k3d or a Hugging Face Space instead of AWS. CI runs unit + data + model tests (metric threshold + one invariance test) and a Compose integration test. A scheduled workflow retrains and promotes only if the challenger beats the champion on the agreed metric.
practice.done_when: Actions history shows one CT run that promoted and one that refused promotion (logged reason); invariance test fails if you deliberately leak a name feature; `make test` runs everything locally.

quiz.prompt: An invariance test checks that:
options: Irrelevant input changes (e.g. names) do not change predictions
quiz.explain: Behavioural tests from CheckList-style testing.

quiz.prompt: A champion/challenger gate promotes when:
options: The challenger beats the champion on agreed metrics and slices
quiz.explain: Promotion must be evidence-based and logged.

quiz.prompt: In ML, CT stands for:
quiz.explain: Automated retraining in production on new data.

quiz.prompt: Why might a model pass its tests in CI but still fail in production?
rubric: Test data not representative / production distribution drift.
Train/serve skew or upstream data changes.
Load/latency/integration issues not covered; slices not tested.

practice.brief: No-card path: k3d + Traefik/nginx Ingress. Run model v1 and v2 as two Deployments with a 90/10 weighted split; additionally mirror 100% of traffic to v2 in shadow mode and log both predictions. Roll back by changing weights only.

quiz.prompt: Shadow deployment:
options: Serves users from the new model
Runs the new model on live traffic without affecting responses
Is the same as a canary
quiz.explain: Zero user impact; compare outputs offline.

quiz.prompt: A canary is judged on:
options: Error rate, latency and quality/business metrics vs the control
quiz.explain: Compare against the stable version under the same traffic.

quiz.prompt: Blue/green enables:
options: An instant switch and instant rollback between two full environments
quiz.explain: Two complete environments; the router flips.

quiz.prompt: Why is shadow testing harder for LLM chat than for a classifier?
rubric: No single correct output; comparison needs evals/LLM-judge or human review.
Non-determinism means differences are expected; stateful multi-turn conversations diverge.
Shadow calls double cost; side-effecting tool calls must be disabled.

practice.title: Catch injected drift (original M16 gate)
practice.brief: No-card path: the module's Docker Compose stack runs fully locally. Generate an Evidently drift report (reference vs current), push drift share and per-slice error to Prometheus (or the module's Postgres), alert in Grafana. Inject drift (shift a feature by +2 sd) and catch it.
practice.done_when: Grafana alert screenshot fires within one evaluation window of the injected batch; the clean batch did not fire; README states thresholds and why; a slice panel shows the subgroup most affected.

quiz.prompt: Concept drift means:
quiz.explain: P(y|x) changes; data drift is P(x).

quiz.prompt: With delayed labels, the earliest signal is usually:
quiz.explain: You can measure inputs/outputs immediately; accuracy waits for labels.

quiz.prompt: Slice metrics matter because:
options: Aggregate metrics can hide failures on subgroups
quiz.explain: A stable average can mask a collapsing segment.

quiz.prompt: Data drift is detected but accuracy is unchanged. What do you do?
rubric: Check whether drifted features matter (importance) and whether labels have matured.
Investigate the cause (upstream change, seasonality, new segment) and slices.
Adjust thresholds or schedule retraining; don't retrain blindly; document the decision.

rubric: Continuously add real failures/user reports from traces.

capstone.title: End-to-end versioned ML pipeline (superset of the Zoomcamp final project)
capstone.brief: Prefect flow: ingest -> validate (Pandera) -> features -> train -> MLflow registry; champion/challenger gate in CI; containerised service plus batch scoring; canary on k3d; Evidently + Prometheus/Grafana drift alert caught on injected drift; retraining policy and postmortem. LLMOps extension (required for AI-engineer track): Langfuse traces + CI eval gate on an LLM feature. No-card path: everything runs locally (MLflow, MinIO/LocalStack, Prefect server, k3d, Grafana) with GitHub Actions; public demo on a Hugging Face Docker Space. Reference: https://github.com/DataTalksClub/mlops-zoomcamp/tree/main/07-project

levels: Fresh clone + `make all` rebuilds data, model and service; data/model version traceable from any prediction
Scheduled/backfillable flow; CI tests code/data/model; automatic logged promotion gate
Canary or shadow rollout plus one-command rollback demonstrated on video
Injected drift triggers an alert; dashboard shows service and model metrics; runbook exists
README explains tool choices, what was skipped (e.g. feature store) and why, cost and known failure modes
